title: Tackling the Objective Inconsistency Problem in Heterogeneous Federated Optimization
layout_note: The two cases are stacked vertically, not side by side: the heterogeneous setting on top, the homogeneous setting below, separated by a grey dashed horizontal rule; each is a sketch of the same parameter space.
grouping: No containers; the dashed rule splits the two settings, each titled at its top right in plain serif text ('Heterogeneous setting', 'Homogeneous setting'). Marker shape and colour separate the kinds of point: blue triangles for the local optima, a green square for the global optimum, black dots for the start and server points.
shapes_depth: Flat vector sketch: a black dot for the shared start x^(t,0); solid blue arrow chains for each client's local steps (in the upper copy client 1's chain is much longer than client 2's); blue dashed arrows from the start to the averaged point; a red dashed line joining the clients' end points, with the server point x^(t+1,0) as a black dot on it. Bold italic math labels beside every point.
proposed_highlight: No method is shown; the two copies carry the argument: with unequal numbers of local steps (top) the averaged point lands far from the global optimum x*, with equal steps (bottom) close to it.
lesson: Show the bias of averaging unequal local progress by drawing the same parameter space twice, stacked - one client's step chain much longer in the upper copy - with the client end points joined by a red dashed line on which the server point sits, against fixed local and global optimum markers.
notes: Venue and year as recorded by Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar); the arXiv v1 PDF names no venue. refs crop found no 'Figure 1' caption (the figure is wrapped beside body text), so page 2 was rendered at 200 dpi with pdftoppm and the figure cut out above its caption (crops/2007.07481/fig1.png in the federated kb-build work dir); pdfimages lists no embedded images on that page, so the crop's figN.json records images_px [] and photo_share is 0. elements 'other' = the optimum markers (triangles, square) in parameter space.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: illustrating objective inconsistency of federated averaging under heterogeneous local steps
taxonomy.note: modality multi = no data modality is drawn; the figure is an abstract parameter-space sketch

core.what: The same parameter-space sketch drawn twice, stacked and split by a grey dashed rule: heterogeneous setting (top) versus homogeneous setting (bottom), so where the server point lands relative to x* is compared across the two copies.

relations.form: two unframed copies of one sketch stacked vertically under a dashed horizontal rule, each titled at top right, with the optima markers in the same row positions
local SGD steps drawn as chains of solid blue arrows from the start dot x^(t,0) in parameter space, with the local optima (triangles) and global optimum (square) as markers below
the averaged update is a dashed blue arrow from the start dot to the server dot x^(t+1,0), which sits on the red dashed segment joining the two clients' end points

channels.colour: blue = client-side quantities (step arrows and local optima triangles), green = global optimum, red = the line of possible averages, black = iterates (start and server point)
channels.shape: dot = iterate, triangle = local optimum, square = global optimum
channels.line: solid blue = local steps, dashed blue = averaged server step, red dashed = segment between client end points; grey dashed = panel divider (a fourth line meaning)

quality.strengths: The argument is pure geometry: in the top copy one client's long step chain drags the server dot toward x_1*, in the bottom copy equal chains leave it near the middle; identical marker sets make the two copies directly comparable.
quality.weaknesses: No key for triangles vs square or solid vs dashed arrows; the optima sit well below the trajectories so the distance from x^(t+1,0) to x* that the figure argues about is hard to judge; dashed lines carry three different meanings (average step, segment, divider).

insights.structure: The same parameter-space sketch is drawn twice, stacked and split by a grey dashed horizontal rule, each titled at its top right in serif text ('Heterogeneous setting', 'Homogeneous setting').
insights.data: Points are markers only: black dots for the start x^(t,0) and the server point x^(t+1,0), blue triangles for local optima x_1*, x_2*, a green square for the global optimum x*; client steps are chains of solid blue arrows and the averaged step a dashed blue arrow.
insights.emphasis: No method is shown; the contrast carries the argument - in the top copy one client's step chain is much longer and the server point on the red dashed line lands far from x*, in the bottom copy it lands near it.
insights.flow: In each copy the eye follows the two step chains outward from the start point, then the red dashed line joining their ends, then the server dot on it relative to the optimum markers; top copy first, then bottom.
insights.avoid: No key explains the triangle / square markers or the solid vs dashed blue arrows, and the optimum markers sit far below the trajectories so the distance being argued is hard to judge.

arrangement.units: two unframed copies of the same sketch stacked vertically, separated by a grey dashed horizontal rule and titled at top right
arrangement.shared: identical marker set (local and global optima) in both copies
